title: Ethical Hacker Squad findings artifact
description: The machine-readable half of a deliverable. The markdown report is what a person reads; this is what a pipeline can check, diff between engagements and score. Enumerations are NOT repeated here: status, severity, confidence and verification are validated against the declared regions of references/vocabulary.md, which is their single home.

scope.description: The exact path, repository or authorized target the squad was pointed at.

commit.description: Commit or version of the target, when it has one.

language.description: The language the findings are written in. Identifiers are never translated.

generated_by.description: The skill and version that produced this file.

coverage_declaration.description: What was exercised and what was not, in the words of references/traceability.md.

authorization.description: Reference to the authorization under which remote or active tests were run, when any were.

coverage.description: The inventory, resolved. Every surface named in `inventoried` must appear in exactly one of `read` or `not_read`. A blinded reader test found a report that inventoried a data-access layer, routed to it, and then resolved it as neither - and concluded that silence about SQL injection in that report was not evidence of its absence. Prose could not stop that; this can.

inventoried.description: Every surface the inventory turned up, named as the reader would name it.

read.description: Surfaces actually examined. A finding here is possible; its absence means clean.

not_read.description: Surfaces deliberately not examined. Silence about these is silence, not a clean bill.

unaided_pass.description: What this reviewer would have reported with no corpus at all, written down BEFORE any pack was opened, and then resolved. Measured cause: across eleven runs the corpus arm found the same defects as an unaided engineer and no more, missed one the unaided arm found while having the right file open, and agreed with itself LESS across repeated runs (0.68 against 0.81). The reading those numbers support is that the corpus was substituting for judgement rather than adding to it - what a procedure names got found, what it did not name got bent into the nearest procedure or dropped. This field makes the substitution impossible to perform silently: a candidate that existed before the pack was opened must end up reported or explicitly dropped with a reason, and never merely absent.

candidates.description: Short labels for everything the reviewer judged worth reporting from its own reading, before loading a pack. Empty is a legitimate answer on a small target and must still be stated.

reported.description: Candidates that became findings. Each label here must be carried by some finding's `unaided_label`, so the claim is checkable against the findings themselves.

resolution.description: Why this candidate is not a finding, as a category rather than a mood. Measured cause: when a weaker model ran short of budget, it did not go quiet - it produced confident refutations, twice dismissing a real unbounded allocation, once by asserting the bounds were correct and once by citing the length cap of a different method. Confirming a finding costs every triage rule; dismissing one cost a sentence, and that price difference is a thumb on the scale toward dismissal. Each category below now carries its own evidence requirement.

reason.description: Why the second reading overturned the first. `the pack has no procedure for it` is refused: that case is `ad-hoc`, not absent.

control_at.description: Required when `resolution` is `refuted`: `path:line` of the control that makes the candidate harmless, on the path that reaches the sink. A refutation names where the bound is enforced, exactly as a confirmation names where it is missing. `it looks correct` is not a refutation.

merged_into.description: Required when `resolution` is `merged`: the id of the finding that absorbed this candidate. It must exist in `findings`.

dropped.description: Candidates deliberately not reported, each with the reason the later reading overturned the earlier one.

procedure.description: The pack procedure that produced it, or `ad-hoc` when none applies.

status.description: From vocabulary.md. `candidate` may never appear in a deliverable.

severity.description: From vocabulary.md, judged in this system rather than copied from a tool.

evidence.description: The minimal trace or reproduction, already redacted. Placeholders only: [REDACTED:secret], [REDACTED:pii], [REDACTED:internal-host], [REDACTED:payload].

verification.description: From vocabulary.md, when a fix was verified.

inference.description: Required for `probable`: the one link that was inferred rather than observed.

withdrawn_reason.description: Required for `withdrawn`: why a claim already made did not survive.

reason.description: Required whenever the answer is not DOES_NOT_HOLD: the artifact that supports it.

what_would_settle_it.description: Required for `probable`: the artifact, file or symbol that would turn the inference into an observation. A gap named without a way to close it sends the reader nowhere.

unaided_label.description: The label this finding carried in `engagement.unaided_pass.candidates`, when it originated there rather than from a procedure. It is the join that lets a validator prove nothing found before the pack was opened went missing after.

duplicate_of.description: The id of the finding this one was merged into. The absorbed finding stays here with its own id; it is rendered under its parent rather than deleted. Requires `merge_rules` with every DUP rule answered and none HOLDS.

possible_duplicate_of.description: Ids this finding may be the same as, where a DUP rule was answered UNKNOWN. Both findings ship and both are counted. This is the state for not having decided, and it carries no proof obligation - charging for it would push work toward the merge.

reason.description: Required whenever the answer is not DOES_NOT_HOLD: the artifact that supports it.

merge_rules.description: Required with `duplicate_of`: the DUP rules of triage.md, answered. Same shape as `triage`.

ruled_out.description: What was tested and did not appear, and what actively resisted. The section a client almost never receives.

outcome.description: From the verification vocabulary: refuted, inconclusive, not executed or blocked.

where.description: What was exercised and how far it reached. A bound, not a claim about the whole system.
